participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, running the meeting)
summary: Standard daily sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan: wins round, month-end projections by person, then a live group review of one of Richard's objection-handling calls. Projections were 20 units / $80K pacing on target; Andrew needed $3,800 more to hit $50K, Richard was told he needed roughly $9,000 more, and Kim needed six more sets to hit 25. Chris flagged that next month's target will be about half, and that an overflow closer is being added to cover holidays without taking calls from the current team. The bulk of the call was coaching Richard on a lost deal: the diagnosis was that he never secured a genuine commitment in discovery and then leaned in too hard during objection handling, and the prescription was 'oak tree energy' — stay neutral, slow down, use silence, and let the prospect introspect rather than pushing. Chris also gave scripted language for the payment question ('most people take care of it up front and throw it on a credit card, why do you ask?'), and side topics covered Skool welcome posts, moderator access for closers, Sunday call blocks, Primal University, and branded merch.
notable: Stated payment default: Chris coached the exact wording for the price-terms question — 'most people take care of it up front and throw it on a credit card. Why do you ask?' — and warned against 'usually it's just a one-time fee' because it implies a recurring charge. Pay-in-full on a credit card is the taught default. Richard had conceded a 50/50 instalment split on his own call the previous day.

Chris on a diabetic prospect who had booked with a diabetes-specialist trainer: he characterised the specialist's differentiation as 'not true', said that as long as insulin is 'in check' the prospect just 'needs to move more and eat less', and asserted 'that's exactly what the primal nutrition plan will do for them'. Clinical positioning is being set by the sales manager rather than by a clinician.

A deposit is in the corpus as a live commercial mechanism and appears to count toward units. Richard: 'I was really counting on the one guy... with the deposits, that's just a big bummer'; the prospect is 'barely responding' and Richard's plan is to 'continue to follow up'. Kim independently references it as 'a deposit from me' when accounting for his own sets.

Andrew recounted urinating into a bottle under his desk mid-call rather than pause a sale, explicitly because the prospect was 'very on the fence, so I didn't want to give him any space'. Chris shut it down firmly for this team ('Andrew, don't do that here').

Closers cannot see when a client is granted Skool access, which is blocking the welcome-post routine. Chris said he would ask the team about giving closers moderator access so they can approve members themselves.
Chris confirmed an overflow closer is joining, explicitly reassuring the team it will only absorb ad-driven overflow and holiday cover, not existing calls.
Primal University is discussed as a possible second offer at a $2K price point — 'we're not moving on it yet, but it is interesting' — and would need Trevor's sign-off.

Chris flagged next month's projection will be roughly half of this month's, and asked reps to declare holidays in advance so cover can be arranged. Andrew declared 10-13 July and a hike from 29 July to 11 August; Richard a possible week in September for Mont Blanc.
Recording is clipped at both ends: it opens mid-sentence on Richard debriefing a call, and cuts off at 01:03:43 mid-sentence just as Richard asks Chris to stay on privately.
